newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom off in grey trade, ups issue volume.
newsitem.headline: Telekom off in grey trade, ups issue volume.

text.p: Shares in German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom, to be floated next week, were lower on Monday in unofficial "grey" trade, after Telekom said it had topped up the volume of its share issue.
Dealers said the news had pushed the share price quoted in the unofficial telephone market down to between 33 marks ($21.95) and 33.50 marks, from 34 marks previously.
The grey market refers to the market provided by brokers prior to a formal offering, where shares are sold ahead of the IPO and honoured when the issue takes place.

The price of between 33 marks and 33.50 marks per share still values the Telekom share 12 percent above the higher end of the initial price range for the share, which has been put at between 25 and 30 marks per share.

Telekom said it had increased the volume of the issue to 600 million shares or three billion marks from an originally planned 500 million shares or 2.5 billion marks, while the green shoe, or oversubscription option, was increased to 90 million shares from 75 million.
The Bild-Zeitung newspaper reported on Monday that the sale, due to go ahead on November 18 in Europe's largest ever flotation, was six times oversubscribed.
